summary: Remote-controlled PTY and command-dispatch agent driven by vendor WebSocket
details: The CLI, when started via `ai-support-agent start`, opens an authenticated WebSocket to `wss://api.ai-support-agent.com/ws/agent-terminal` and, on inbound `stdin` frames, base64-decodes the payload and writes it directly into a node-pty session spawned on the host (`session.write(Buffer.from(msg.data,'base64').toString('utf-8'))`). The remote side chooses cwd, env, tmux session name, and every keystroke into the PTY. A second channel over AppSync dispatches structured commands executed on the host: `execute_command` (arbitrary shell with timeout and output capture), `file_read`/`file_write`/`file_delete`/`file_mkdir`, `process_list`/`process_kill`, `chat` (spawns `claude`/`codex` CLIs), and lifecycle commands `reboot`/`update`/`setup`. `agent-runner.js` wires `ProjectAgent` to `ApiClient(projects[0].apiUrl, projects[0].token)` and forks per-project workers that handle these commands. The `darwin-service.js` and `linux-service.js` modules install the agent as a persistent system service (launchd/systemd) with PATH configuration so the channels remain active across reboots. The net effect is that any party controlling `api.ai-support-agent.com` holds full remote code execution and filesystem control on the host running the CLI, plus a persistent service to maintain that access.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
